cues.title: A crystal changes the air
cues.narration: A growing crystal draws water vapour out of the air around it. Near the ice, the supply becomes depleted. The crystal creates an invisible halo around itself.
cues.description: The Run B model grows from its seed to an early plate. No vapour field is shown over this replay.
cues.qualification: The mechanism is sourced separately; this replay does not measure its field or rates. Model ticks are not physical seconds. Thickness is styled at 2.6 times.

cues.title: The invisible supply
cues.narration: Even in still air, random molecular motion carries a net supply inward. These colours show an imagined cross-section of that supply, not something a camera would see.
cues.description: Qualitative contour bands surround a hexagonal ice cross-section. The inward arrows represent net delivery, not individual molecular paths. Closely spaced bands near the ice indicate a changing supply.
cues.qualification: Schematic, not a computed field. No numerical concentration, physical scale or elapsed cloud time is implied.
cues.review: Prototype wording source-checked by non-author research agent; full-script review pending

cues.title: A small advantage
cues.narration: Now add a small bump. In this simplified picture, the vapour gradient is steeper near its tip. More vapour can arrive there, and the bump can grow faster.
cues.description: One corner extends into a protrusion. Contour spacing tightens near its tip and net-delivery arrows gather there. The contours are qualitative; the tip is not labelled as holding the most vapour.
cues.qualification: Simplified diffusion-limited surface. This is the geometric feedback in the source, not a simulation or measured flux.
cues.review: Prototype wording source-checked by non-author research agent; full-script review pending

cues.title: Growth feeds growth
cues.narration: That makes it stick out farther, increasing its advantage. This is the branching instability. Surface attachment can oppose it, so a bump does not always become a branch.
cues.description: The protrusion extends, then holds while the opposing role of surface attachment appears. The diagram does not make every perturbation grow or turn all corners into branches.
cues.qualification: Surface attachment can resist the diffusion-driven feedback. Not every bump becomes a branch.

cues.title: The shape we want to explain
cues.narration: Now return to our computer-grown crystal. Its branches illustrate the shape we are trying to understand. This replay is model output, not proof of the explanation.
cues.description: The schematic disappears completely before the Run B replay resumes from its held early state and grows toward its final silhouette.
cues.qualification: Model output, unvalidated. No temperature, supersaturation or physical growth seconds are assigned to G-G ticks.
